Ikea and City Energy partner to integrate gas appliances into home design service
article:
Ikea Singapore has partnered Life by City Energy, the home solutions arm of town gas provider City Energy, to incorporate gas appliances and installation planning into the furnishing retailer’s Home Design Service.

The collaboration allows homeowners to plan their kitchen cabinetry, appliance placement and gas piping requirements together before renovation begins.

Life by City Energy is the first partner to expand Ikea's Home Design Service, which was launched in 2025.

Under the arrangement, homeowners can select gas hobs, cooker hoods, gas water heaters and dryers from Life by City Energy as part of their home design plans.

An Ikea Home Design specialist will remain the homeowner's main point of contact, coordinating with Life by City Energy's specialists on appliance specifications, gas piping requirements and installation.

Once homeowners proceed with their design proposal, site visits and technical checks will be arranged where necessary. Ikea will handle cabinetry and appliance positioning, while Life by City Energy will arrange appliance delivery, installation and gas connections through its teams and partners.

Previously, homeowners using the Home Design Service had to source gas appliances separately and provide their specifications before kitchen plans could be finalised.

The partnership aims to reduce the need for separate arrangements and minimise potential installation delays or mismatched specifications.

“By bringing Life by City Energy solutions into that journey, customers can now bring their gas appliances and requirements into that conversation earlier, too, so more of the home can be planned together from the start,” said Steve Croasdale, commercial manager for Ikea Singapore, in a November 2026 press release

Soh Guan Hong, senior vice-president of residential sales at City Energy, said:  “With town gas infrastructure available in all new HDB flats, gas remains an integral part of Singapore's residential infrastructure, serving daily cooking, water heating and even laundry drying needs.”

The expanded Home Design Service is available at Ikea Alexandra and Ikea Tampines.

title: What's moving the market: Singapore's biggest property deals and hottest searches (Nov 13)
article:
Here is this week’s data-led look at Singapore’s property market, covering record transactions, rental benchmarks and the most searched homes on EdgeProp.

The following insights are compiled from EdgeProp Buddy , URA Realis and data.gov.sg, downloaded as of Nov 10.

Non-landed private homes — new launches, resales and rents

By transaction volume, Thomson Reserve saw the highest activity among new launch condos in the past fortnight to Nov 10, with 1,122 deals recorded.

The mega project, with over a thousand homes, debuted on Oct 31 with a take-up rate exceeding 90% at its VIP preview and launch day.

Lucerne Grand in Jurong West, Union Square Residences along Havelock Road, and Dunearn House on Dunearn Road were next on the list with 27, 24 and 21 transactions respectively.

All 10 of the most expensive condo units sold in the past fortnight also came from Thomson Reserve, involving homes on the highest floors.

Topping the list was a 30th-storey apartment fetching close to $5.98 million or $3,306 psf.

Following closely were a 29th-storey unit at nearly $5.96 million and a 28th-storey unit at around $5.94 million.

In the condo rental market, a unit at Meyerhouse in the Tanjong Katong area is being leased out for $21,500 per month, placing it among the highest rents in the Rest of Central Region (RCR) or city fringe.

Units at Riviere along Jiak Kim Street and Coastline Residences in the East Coast area also made the list with monthly rents of $18,000 and $14,000 respectively.

Landed homes — highest transacted prices and rents

In the Caldecott Hill Estate Good Class Bungalow (GCB) area, in District 11, a landed home along Olive Road was resold for $26.75 million. That works out to $1,467 psf based on its freehold land area of 18,241 sq ft.

Another GCB area yielded the next priciest deal in the landed property segment. A house on Oriole Crescent in the Raffles Park GCB area went for $24.5 million, or $2,411 psf on its freehold site area of 10,163 sq ft.

As for the leasing market in the RCR, the highest monthly rent achieved by a landed house was $31,000 or $4.96 psf. The detached house on Broadrick Road, off Mountbatten Road near the East Coast, measures around 6,250 sq ft.

Meanwhile, a terraced house along Race Course Road in Farrer Park is bringing in $27,000 a month, and a detached house on Jalan Kampong Chantek in Bukit Timah is fetching $20,000 a month.

HDB flats — top prices and rents, most transacted blocks

The public housing resale market saw a new islandwide record-high transaction price when a five-room flat in Dawson fetched $1.818 million on Oct 30. It is part of the SkyParc @ Dawson development, on the 40th to 42nd storeys.

The seller’s agent, Ted Wong of ERA, told EdgeProp Singapore that more than eight offers were received from prospective buyers.

The highest rents for HDB flats in the last 14 days stood at between $4,900 to $5,500 per month.

A three-room flat on Lim Liak Street in Bukit Merah took pole position, followed by a five-room flat along Clementi Avenue 3 with a $5,100 monthly rent.

title: ST Engineering Share Price: Is This Defence Stock Still Worth Buying?
article:
Singapore Technologies Engineering
(SGX: S63), or ST Engineering, has
rallied strongly
over the past few years.
Rising defence budgets and the steady commercial aerospace sector explain much of the share price gain.
But after a staggering run like this, how much of the future is already reflected in the share price?
In this article, we evaluate whether today’s valuation is justified by the business, or if you can afford to wait for better opportunities.
ST Engineering: More Than Just a Defence Stock
ST Engineering has a nicely diversified business across three main segments: Commercial Aerospace (CA), Defence & Public Security (DPS), and Urban Solutions & Satcom (USS).
Its CA segment provides aftermarket maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) services for, as you might guess, commercial aircrafts.
As Singapore’s prime defence major, ST Engineering also provides defence equipment, military systems and security solutions for governments and armed forces worldwide through its DPS segment.
Finally, USS covers smart city systems, transport technology and satellite communications.
Overall, these businesses provide different economic exposures and ensure ST Engineering does not solely rely on a particular industry.
Much of the work also runs on long contracts with governments and airlines, which make future revenue more predictable compared to other companies.
Why Is Driving ST Engineering’s Growth?
Defence spending is the
headline driver
.
Global military spending has risen over recent years, as countries increasingly look to upgrade their defence capabilities given the conflicts in Russia/Ukraine and the Middle East.
This trend, unlikely to slow anytime soon, plays into ST Engineering’s DPS segment, which has benefitted from more contracts for defence and military solutions.
Aircraft maintenance is the quieter one.
Like defence, global spending on MRO activities has picked up as global aircraft fleets age and require more maintenance and upkeep work.
This dual engine has resulted in a steadily increasing order book for ST Engineering.
As of 30 June 2026 (1H2026), the order book hit a record S$35.7 billion, up 14% from a year earlier, with S$5.7 billion due to be delivered in the rest of 2026.
Given the group’s FY2025 (ending 31 December 2025) total revenue of S$12.35 billion, the current order book provides close to three years of revenue visibility.
That said, a big order doesn’t automatically guarantee big profits.
Execution risk still matters, and higher costs could whittle down the margins of each contract, ultimately resulting in lower profits.
Are ST Engineering’s Earnings Keeping Up with Its Share Price?
So far, yes.
In 1H2026, revenue rose 11% to S$6.6 billion and net profit climbed 27% to S$512 million, so earnings are growing faster than sales.
CA led the way, with operating profit up 29%. DPS grew 10%, and USS almost quadrupled its operating profit (albeit from a low base) after cost cuts.
Cash is coming in too.
Operating cash flow rose 26% to S$960 million, and free cash flow improved to S$591.6 million from S$591.6 million from S$484.6 million.
Meanwhile, debt looks manageable.
Borrowings were S$4.7 billion against S$255.3 million of cash and cash equivalents as of 30 June 2026, with the group steadily deleveraging across the past year.
Is ST Engineering’s Current Valuation Justified?
This is where it gets harder.
As at 12 November 2026, ST Engineering trades at trailing and forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios of 57.1x and 26.1x, respectively.
Against their historical averages, these earnings ratios seem stretched.
The market is clearly paying up for defence exposure and earnings visibility.
If profit growth slows, the multiple could shrink, with the share price going nowhere even while the underlying business keeps doing well.
ST Engineering’s new dividend policy dictates a base dividend of S$0.18 per share for 2026 plus about a third of any rise in underlying profit per share.
Interim payments of S$0.04 and S$0.05 have been made so far.
Free cash flow of S$591.6 million in 1H2026 comfortably covered the S$468.2 million paid out in dividends during the half.
But at S$9.74 (as at 12 November 2026), the trailing yield is roughly 2.5%, which does not scream attractive to income investors.
What Could Drive ST Engineering’s Next Phase of Growth?
More defence contracts from an international pipeline, additional aircraft maintenance capacity and increasing profit contribution from USS could help.
Continued conversion of order backlogs to underlying profits and cash flows, alongside any improvements in operating margins, will be beneficial for ST Engineering as well.
The key risks for the group include delays or cost overruns on big projects, weaker margins and slower contract wins.
Already, new orders in 1H2026 were S$7.6 billion, down from S$9.1 billion a year earlier.
Get Smart: A Strong Business, but Is the Price Right?
Undoubtedly, ST Engineering is a well-diversified group that benefits from strong spending in
global defence
and commercial aerospace.
A S$35.7 billion order book provides good revenue visibility moving forward, but execution risk could still present a possible concern for future profit and cash generation.
However, the current price already reflects most of that.
Current valuations leave little room for disappointment.
Long-term investors who like the business would do better waiting for a more reasonable valuation, or building a position gradually over time.

title: Carlsberg said set to start road show for US$600 mil India IPO — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): Carlsberg A/S is set to start investor meetings as early as next week for an initial public offering (IPO) of its India business that could raise as much as US$600 million, according to people familiar with the matter.

Carlsberg India Ltd, the country’s second-largest brewer, could launch the IPO as early as January, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. The Danish brewer is seeking a valuation of US$4 billion for the India business, the people said.

Deliberations are ongoing and details including the size, structure and timing of the transaction could still change, the people said. A representative for Carlsberg declined to comment.

The proposed offering would consist entirely of a secondary share sale by the Danish parent. Carlsberg entity South Asian Breweries Pte Ltd plans to sell as many as 86.42 million shares, representing 15% of the company’s equity capital, according to the prospectus. Carlsberg confidentially submitted draft IPO documents in July and made its filing public on Oct 27.

Carlsberg has appointed Kotak Mahindra Capital Co, Citigroup Inc and JPMorgan Chase & Co to manage the offering, the prospectus shows.

Strong demand for Jio Platforms Ltd’s record US$3.1 billion IPO and its post-listing performance have boosted confidence among prospective issuers looking to press ahead with large transactions. Investors’ ability to absorb such offerings could encourage more companies waiting on the sidelines to accelerate their listing plans, potentially keeping India among the world’s busiest markets for new share sales into 2027.

See also: Bankers looking at raising Anthropic's valuation to US$1.5 tril or more — FT

Carlsberg India reported revenue of 87.09 billion rupees for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026. The company operates seven breweries and had a 21.9% market share across 16 key states and union territories in fiscal 2026, according to the prospectus.

title: ST Engineering wins initial 'low rate' order for land system platform from defence customer in Europe
article:
Singapore Technologies Engineering has won an initial "low rate" production order for a land systems platform.

The customer is in Europe and the company is hopeful that orders for the full production may follow in the "not too distant" future.

Winning this contract for a land platform is in contrast to other recent overseas defence orders, such as recurring ammunition orders, and more recently, maintenance orders.

ST Engineering's executives, for now, are not saying what kind of product this is, and who the customer is.

However, they stress that this is a significant development.

"This is a validation of the quality and capabilities of our platform and hopefully, the initial vanguard to much larger orders subsequently," says Mervyn Tan, the company's group chief operating officer.

See also: Sats reports 2QFY2027 earnings of $81.1 mil, up 2.8% y-o-y

The key land system platforms built by the company, and which is being marketed around, include various versions of the Terrex family of infantry fighting vehicles, and also the Bronco all-terrain-track-carrier.

Vincent Chong, the company's group president and CEO, points out that this particular platform is also in the run for similar contracts in other markets.

This means if ST Engineering can win orders from other customers as well, it is able to enjoy operational efficiencies.

This aside, in the third quarter of the year, ST Engineering won defence and public security orders worth $1.8 billion, with a total haul of $5.6 billion. Total order book is now at a record level of $37.7 billion.

title: Microsoft tries to fix Outlook and Copilot hours into outage
article:
(Nov 13): Microsoft Corp is struggling to restore access to some of its flagship software more than nine hours after an outage began, leaving users unable to use email and chat services in one of the tech giant’s most severe disruptions in recent memory.

Outlook, Teams and the Copilot artificial intelligence service were unavailable for most of the US workday on Thursday for some users. Microsoft’s products are among the most widely used software among business, government and educational institutions.

The outage, which attracted about 200,000 reports of user issues across Microsoft services on Downdetector, ranks among the company’s most severe. Previous disruptions have rarely lasted more than several hours. Microsoft shares were down 0.4% in extended trading.

In a series of updates to its status page, the company detailed frustrated efforts to fix its malfunctioning systems and route user traffic away from affected servers. After initially struggling to identify the issue and test potential remedies, the company said in an update that it’s “seeing positive results with our efforts to restart affected infrastructure”.

Though the number of new reports has slowed, services have not been restored.

Citing the outage, Workhorse Group Inc, a truck and bus manufacturer, said it would postpone its earnings release, originally scheduled for Thursday, until Monday. School districts, universities and hospitals were among those warning that communications might be limited.

See also: Nvidia market cap sinks below US$4 tril following Huang's resignation

“We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” the company said in an earlier update. “Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.”

Over the course of the day, the company added to its tally of the number of products users might fail to access. Services for technologists, including cybersecurity software, file-sharing services and administrator tools, were also disrupted.

The company sells those products, along with workplace staples like Word and Excel, in a bundle under the M365 brand.

See also: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress to serve as interim CEO

In a separate post on X earlier on Thursday, Microsoft said users “in any region” could be affected.

The Japanese government’s shared IT platform is also experiencing disruptions, Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki said at a regular press conference.

title: New World considering rights issue as Bain walks away — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): New World Development Co is considering a rights issue to help shore up its finances after Bain Capital decided against investing in the property company, according to people familiar with the situation.

New World may seek to raise as much as HK$25 billion (US$3.2 billion or $4.1 billion) in the potential rights issue, the people said. The indebted developer’s controlling shareholder, the Cheng family, intends to participate and inject fresh capital, the people added, asking not to be identified to discuss private deliberations.

New World’s shares were suspended from trading Friday morning pending an announcement. The shares have fallen 33% this year, leaving the company with a market capitalisation of about HK$12.3 billion.

A rights issue involves a company raising cash by selling new shares to stakeholders at a discount. The banks are considering softly underwriting the share sale, meaning they’ll try to find outside investors instead of promising to buy unsold shares with their own money, the people said.

Deliberations are ongoing and might not result in a rights issue, the people said.

Representatives for New World and the Cheng family didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

See also: Hong Kong listing proceeds hit six-year high, close to record

Bain had been exploring a potential investment in New World but decided against it after failing to agree on terms, people familiar with the situation said, without elaborating. A representative for Bain declined to comment.

Blackstone Inc walked away from a proposed tie-up with New World earlier this year after the Cheng family refused to give up control, Bloomberg News reported in May.

New World reported a record US$3.6 billion ($4.6 billion) fiscal-year loss and has been trying to strengthen its finances after years of liquidity strain caused by the property slump in Hong Kong and mainland China. With significant debt maturing in the coming years, investors are closely focused on its refinancing plans.

See also: New World’s top shareholder seeks bank loan as equity deal looms — Bloomberg

New World chief executive officer Echo Huang told analysts in late September that the developer’s focus was on improving its balance sheet by cutting debt and disposing of assets.

title: US probes if Alice Huang helped smuggle Super Micro products — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): The Justice Department is probing Alice Huang, the woman US officials suspect as a possible spy targeting the ousted head of Nvidia Corp, over whether entities linked to her were involved in efforts to smuggle products made by Super Micro Computer Inc to China, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The previously unreported scrutiny is being led by the US attorney’s office in Manhattan, said the person, who asked not to be identified due to the sensitivity of the matter. It’s unclear whether the probe into Alice Huang is specifically tied to any of the chip smuggling cases already brought by prosecutors in the US or Asia.

The Justice Department is already spearheading an investigation into Alice Huang’s former company Megaspeed International over suspected semiconductor smuggling, Bloomberg News has reported. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing.

Of the cases where charges have been brought, the most prominent involves Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, who along with two others Manhattan federal prosecutors charged in March over an alleged conspiracy to send Nvidia — powered servers to an unnamed Southeast Asian company and then divert them to Chinese customers. Super Micro wasn’t named as a defendant and has said it is cooperating with the investigation. Liaw, who pleaded not guilty, is no longer at the company.

Super Micro declined to comment on prosecutors’ scrutiny of Alice Huang before publication. “Supermicro has been responsive to inquiries and has fully cooperated with US and Taiwanese officials, while also voluntarily providing information and engaging with all requests from Singapore authorities to date,” the company said in a subsequent statement. “Megaspeed is not, and has never been, a Supermicro customer. Supermicro maintains a robust compliance programme and continues to work closely with authorities and industry partners to combat diversion and help protect American innovation.”

Spokespeople for the Justice Department and the Manhattan US attorney’s office also declined to comment. It wasn’t immediately clear what potential role Alice Huang, or entities connected to her, could have played in smuggling Super Micro products into China. Justice Department probes can end without any charges being filed.

See also: Elon Musk says it would be an honour to hire Nvidia’s Huang

Alice Huang is currently living in Beijing with the knowledge of security officials, Bloomberg News has reported, and attempts to reach her were unsuccessful. Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, was in former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang’s orbit through Megaspeed, the largest buyer of Nvidia’s chips in Southeast Asia, Bloomberg News has reported.

The scrutiny from US prosecutors represents another twist in a rapidly unfolding scandal that has engulfed the booming AI industry. The Justice Department is conducting an espionage probe that includes looking at her relationship with Jensen Huang, said the person familiar with the effort.

No conclusions have been reached by the Justice Department around “who she is or is not” regarding whether Alice Huang acted as a Chinese spy, Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday.

See also: Adani eyes mix of equity, debt for US$2.9 bil Evos takeover — Bloomberg

Jensen Huang’s disclosure on Sunday that he had an extramarital affair plunged Nvidia into an unprecedented crisis, fuelling a sharp selloff in the company’s shares and ultimately his ouster as chief executive officer on Thursday. Jensen is not a target of probes by US law enforcement, according to the person familiar with the matter. Jensen and Alice aren’t related.

Deepening scrutiny into her activities also underscores how Jensen Huang’s admission has reverberated between Silicon Valley, Washington and Beijing. China has rejected the spying allegations as a “smear,” but the episode threatens to emerge as an irritant in a high-stakes upcoming meeting between President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping.

Bloomberg News has reported that the unnamed Southeast Asia company referenced in the March indictment was Bangkok-based OBON Corp. OBON hasn’t responded to requests for comment. According to US prosecutors, two unidentified third-party brokers were also involved in diverting servers to China.

“We have taken action against all identified employees and those parties no longer have any relationship with Supermicro,” chief executive officer Charles Liang said in a public letter to stakeholders in March. “Mr Wally Liaw has also resigned from the company’s board of directors.”

Super Micro said in August, following an independent probe, that its current senior management had no knowledge of the alleged scheme.

title: Samsung in talks to acquire data centre cooling firm Modine — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 13): Samsung Electronics Co is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing Co, a maker of cooling systems for data centres, according to people familiar with the matter.

The companies are discussing a potential transaction that could come together as soon as the coming weeks, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private.

Modine’s shares closed regular trading Thursday in New York at US$106.10, giving the company a market value of about US$5.6 billion. The stock soared to more than US$135 in late trading, a gain of 28%.

The company’s shares had fallen about 15% since Nov 3, when it reported quarterly results that underwhelmed investors. No final decision has been made and the talks could still fall apart, the people said. Another suitor could also emerge, they added.

The discussions underscore how M&A is picking up around companies that cater to the booming AI market. US companies and their overseas rivals have stepped up efforts to capture the growth opportunity coming from data centres through bigger investments and dealmaking. Among them are Samsung’s Asian rivals Daikin Industries Ltd and LG Electronics Inc, as well as US-based Vertiv Holdings Co.

Representatives for Samsung and Modine declined to comment.

See also: Unilever-McCormick deal facing in-depth review from UK watchdog

Based in Racine, Wisconsin, Modine makes heavy duty cooling and heating systems for large commercial buildings and industrial machines, with its fastest-growing business serving hyperscalers that build data centres. In October, the company spun off its automotive business to focus on its thermal-management operations.

Samsung, with a market value of more than US$900 billion, is one of the largest technology and electronics companies in the world. The Suwon, South Korea-based company’s products include smartphones, televisions, home appliances, thermal solutions and computer memory chips.

While a Modine takeover would be bolder in magnitude, Samsung has been bolstering its thermal solutions offering to data centres through international acquisitions. It purchased Germany-based FläktGroup Holding GmbH for €1.5 billion (US$1.7 billion) last year.

title: Asian stocks gain after Nvidia upheaval, oil holds
article:
(Nov 13): Asian stocks climbed as investors eased back into technology shares amid fading concerns that a leadership crisis at Nvidia Corp may derail the broader artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Oil steadied.

The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 1%, led by gains in South Korea and Taiwan as shares in regional tech giants Samsung Electronics Co, SK Hynix Inc and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co advanced. US equity-index futures also climbed, with Nasdaq 100 contracts up 0.6% and S&P 500 futures gaining 0.4% after both benchmarks fell Thursday.

Nvidia, the company at the heart of the AI boom, dropped as much as 14% after chief executive officer Jensen Huang was ousted, but dip buyers stepped in, leaving it just 4.3% lower by the close.

Global benchmark Brent crude steadied just below US$96 a barrel after rising Thursday as President Donald Trump said the US could forgo a deal with Iran. Treasury yields mostly held near Thursday’s highs as traders braced for faster Federal Reserve rate hikes, while a gauge of dollar strength was little changed. Gold steadied after a three-session decline and bitcoin traded around US$71,100.

The upheaval at Nvidia is testing the AI trade without derailing the broader investment boom. Instead, it may make investors more selective, favouring companies best placed to benefit from continued spending.

“This is going to be a more differentiated story and players that have stronger balance sheets that are more focused on doing the hard work of that community engagement are likely to be the winners in this next stage of the buildout,” Mike Pyle, deputy head of BlackRock’s Portfolio Management Group, said in an interview on Bloomberg Television.

See also: Asian stocks edge higher, shrug off Nvidia woes

That shift was already evident on Wall Street. Shares of Broadcom Inc and Advanced Micro Devices Inc, which compete with Nvidia in parts of the AI chip market, rallied over 5% as investors sought potential beneficiaries from the industry leader’s setback.

Nvidia’s market capitalisation briefly dropped below US$4 trillion ($5.2 trillion) with revelations about Huang’s extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, rattling investors ahead of earnings. A related probe into suspected spy Alice Huang and efforts to smuggle Super Micro Computer Inc products to China sent that company’s shares down as much as 16%, the most in more than five months.

“Nvidia’s earnings already demand close attention, but they will be under an even brighter spotlight next week,” said Bret Kenwell at eToro. “Investors will be looking to Nvidia for a fresh read on demand and a reason to regain confidence.”

See also: Asian stocks rise on AI enthusiasm, bonds decline

Two other events next week may provide a broader test of appetite for the AI trade: Anthropic PBC’s highly anticipated IPO and CoreWeave Inc’s plan to raise at least US$4 billion through an investment-grade loan offering. Strong institutional demand for Anthropic suggests appetite for AI exposure remains robust.

In Asia, traders will also be watching the yen after it weakened past 160 per dollar for the first time since September, reviving the prospect that Japanese authorities may intervene to support the currency.

“Markets are jittery about potential FX intervention whenever we approach the 160 area,” said Win Thin, chief economist at Bank of Nassau 1982.

Higher oil prices added to pressure on Treasuries, extending a sell-off sparked Tuesday by hotter-than-expected inflation and signals that Fed officials may favour more aggressive rate hikes. Policy-sensitive two-year yields edged lower after climbing 14 basis points on Thursday.

On Thursday, New York Fed president John Williams said that US inflation remains high and that policymakers have to take further action to contain price pressures.

“Investors continue to pencil in more rate hikes,” said Gennadiy Goldberg, head of US interest rates strategy at TD Securities. While setbacks for US technology shares — which benefited Treasuries last month — “could short-circuit the bearish move at some point, the macro underpinnings are the ones driving Treasuries right now”.

title: Ex-Malaysia digital star that built PM’s avatar is mired in debt
article:
(Nov 13): Earlier this year, Malaysia’s Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) was preparing to list its artificial intelligence unit on Nasdaq and had even built an AI avatar of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Now the onetime digital infrastructure star has lost more than 90% of its market value, is mired in debt and risks defaulting on its Islamic bonds.

Valued at RM10.5 billion (US$2.6 billion) at its peak in 2018, Zetrix’s market capitalisation has plunged to around RM430 million as the company that once held a near-monopoly on providing online state services struggles to diversify its business. Its grip on government contracts began loosening in 2023 as Malaysia shifted away from exclusive concessions to state-run services and competing platforms.

The company’s troubles deepened last month when authorities suspended its remaining online road tolls collection service after saying Zetrix owed the government RM314 million in Road Transport Department fees dating from May 19 to Sept 30.

“We are confident we will weather this,” founder Wong Thean Soon said in an emailed response to questions. “We take a long-term view and understand the market is adjusting to our transition from a primarily Malaysian government-focused business to a more international” one.

In its former guise as MyEG Services Bhd, the company oversaw government online services such as road tax renewals, traffic summons payments and foreign worker permits. As it began losing its exclusive rights to those services, it pivoted to AI and blockchain and started seeking new revenue abroad. It changed its name to Zetrix last year.

See also: Johor property prices rise as demand favours homes near RTS Link

When the value of the company’s stock plunged, Wong was forced to sell 2.22 billion of his Zetrix shares between June and October to meet margin calls on his stock-based loans, ending his role as Zetrix’s largest shareholder. That put the company at risk of breaching its Islamic bonds covenant, which requires Wong to remain Zetrix’s biggest owner.

MARC Ratings subsequently cut the company’s debt score to one rung above default on the risk bondholders could declare a nonpayment. Zetrix, in a filing on Tuesday, said it owed RM25 million in bond payments due Nov 6.

Bursa Malaysia extended its deadline for Zetrix to disclose additional financial information from Wednesday to Nov 13. “The company will take the necessary steps to ensure compliance with the directive within the extended timeframe,” Zetrix said Wednesday.

See also: SoftBank, Grab and PETROS lock in US$1.85 bil seed capital for AI infrastructure in Malaysia

The company’s immediate priorities are to fulfill its obligations and strengthen financial and operational positions, Wong said. Zetrix is banking on its domestic and foreign investments in AI and blockchain to generate new business, he said.

“We endeavor to exceed the previous all-time high because the blockchain and AI growth is still in its nascent stage,” he said of the company’s market value.

Meanwhile, the Anwar avatar that acts as a chatbot for queries from the public has also created complications. The service was indefinitely suspended just days after its July 19 launch when users forced the chatbot to make political statements, some of which were critical of the prime minister.

Wong said Zetrix is working with the premier’s team on new guardrails for the chatbot before reactivating it.

The founder acknowledged that recent developments are weighing on market confidence.

“The group is taking concrete actions and making responsible decisions to reinforce financial discipline, strengthen governance and ensure business continuity,” Wong said.
